questions.question_text: What is the primary defining characteristic of Generative AI compared to traditional artificial intelligence systems?

options.D: It strictly operates by executing predefined, hard-coded if-then logic rules created by human programmers.
options.A: It creates new and original content, such as text, images, or audio, by learning patterns from existing data.
options.B: It replaces rule-based relational databases with deterministic search algorithms.
options.C: It focuses exclusively on sorting and labeling structured tabular numerical data without pattern recognition.

questions.explanation: Generative AI is a subset of artificial intelligence that uses deep learning models to produce novel content—such as text, images, audio, synthetic data, and code—by identifying and replicating patterns learned from training data. Traditional AI and predictive models typically analyze, categorize, or make predictions on existing data rather than generating brand-new artifacts.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the hierarchical relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Generative AI (GenAI)?

options.C: Artificial Intelligence is the broad umbrella, Machine Learning is a subset of AI, Deep Learning is a subset of ML, and Generative AI is a subset of Deep Learning.
options.D: Deep Learning and Generative AI are completely unrelated fields outside the scope of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.
options.B: Generative AI is the broadest umbrella term, with Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning nested inside it.
options.A: Machine Learning encompasses Artificial Intelligence, which contains Generative AI, which contains Deep Learning.

questions.explanation: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the broad umbrella discipline for building intelligent systems. Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI focused on learning from data. Deep Learning (DL) is a specialized subset of ML that uses multi-layered neural networks. Generative AI (GenAI) is built on deep learning architectures to generate new content.

questions.question_text: How does a generative model differ fundamentally from a discriminative model in machine learning?

options.C: A generative model only works with structured numerical tables, whereas a discriminative model only processes unstructured text.
options.A: A generative model evaluates pre-existing labels on data, whereas a discriminative model generates synthetic media from scratch.
options.B: A generative model learns the underlying distribution to produce new data instances, whereas a discriminative model learns decision boundaries to classify or predict labels for given data.
options.D: A generative model requires deterministic rules without training data, whereas a discriminative model requires neural networks.

questions.explanation: Discriminative models learn decision boundaries between classes to categorize inputs or predict labels (e.g., classifying whether an email is spam). Generative models learn the underlying probability distribution of the data to create new, realistic samples that resemble the training data.

questions.question_text: A business leader wants to identify an appropriate use case for Generative AI within customer support operations. Which of the following tasks is the best fit for Generative AI?

options.C: Drafting contextual, natural-sounding email responses and summarizing lengthy customer inquiry threads.
options.A: Calculating the exact monthly billing total for a customer based on fixed subscription rates.
options.B: Storing encrypted customer credit card information securely in a relational database.
options.D: Routing a network packet to the nearest physical data center using static routing tables.

questions.explanation: Drafting contextual conversational responses and synthesizing long unstructured documents (summarization) are primary use cases for Generative AI models like Large Language Models (LLMs). Exact arithmetic, secure database storage, and network packet routing rely on deterministic, rule-based systems where generative models are not suitable.

questions.question_text: An organization is evaluating potential AI initiatives. Which scenario represents a standard use case for Generative AI rather than traditional predictive machine learning?

options.C: Forecasting next quarter's inventory demand using historical time-series sales figures.
options.A: Predicting whether a bank transaction is fraudulent based on historical numerical transaction features.
options.B: Generating synthetic photo-realistic product images and marketing ad copy for an upcoming product launch.
options.D: Classifying incoming support tickets into predetermined priority categories like 'Low', 'Medium', or 'High'.

questions.explanation: Synthesizing photo-realistic images and authoring marketing copy are quintessential generative tasks that create novel content. In contrast, predicting fraudulent transactions (binary classification), forecasting sales (regression/time-series), and categorizing tickets into predetermined priorities (classification) are standard predictive machine learning tasks.

Discriminative models learn decision boundaries between classes to categorize inputs or predict labels (e.g., classifying whether an email is spam). Generative models learn the underlying probability distribution of the data to create new, realistic samples that resemble the training data.
